review_notes: I read the whole file and looked at its simp calls. I grepped Mathlib for existing simp or canonical lemmas about idempotence of `Pi.single i 1` and found none. I also checked the `Pi.single_mul` and `Pi.single_mul_left` lemmas in Algebra/GroupWithZero/Pi.lean. I did not look closely at the `simp_rw +instances [RingHom.coe_coe]` call, which looks like a local instance-transparency issue and not a simp-set problem. I did not run Lean, so I have not checked that the proposed lemma compiles or that making it simp causes no downstream conflicts.

findings.problem: Showing that `Pi.single i 1` is idempotent needs a hand-built simp call. The call unfolds `IsIdempotentElem` and rewrites with `← Pi.single_mul_left`. That rewrite runs in the reverse direction and is not a simp lemma, so the call depends on the exact syntactic shape of the goal. The same ad hoc call appears in at least three other files, and one of them uses `← Pi.single_mul`. Mathlib has no canonical simp lemma for `IsIdempotentElem (Pi.single i 1)`, so a nearby `simp` call cannot discharge it without unfolding the definition and supplying a reversed rewrite.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma such as `Pi.isIdempotentElem_single (i : ι) : IsIdempotentElem (Pi.single i (1 : α i))`, tagged `@[simp]` if it is accepted as a canonical form. Its proof would be the existing `by simp [IsIdempotentElem, ← Pi.single_mul]`. Each caller, including this one, would then use `by simp` or the lemma name directly, with no unfolding and no reversed `Pi.single_mul` rewrite.
findings.benefit: Callers no longer repeat a fragile unfold-and-reverse-rewrite recipe. Idempotence of `Pi.single i 1` becomes available to `simp` and to discoverability tools. It also avoids the reversed `Pi.single_mul_left` rewrite, which could loop if it were ever made a simp lemma.
